Rashi on Gittin 70b:10:1.hebrew: צילותא היא - צלולה היה דעתו, אלא שכחש כחו מלהוציא דבר בפיו:
Rashi on Gittin 70b:10:1.english: [His mind] is lucid - His mind was lucid, except that his strength had weakened [preventing him] from uttering a word with his mouth.

Rashi on Gittin 70b:10:2.hebrew: שגישתא - תרגום של "מהומה", כלומר דעת מבולבל:
Rashi on Gittin 70b:10:2.english: Shegishta [confused] - [This is the Aramaic] Targum [translation] of "mehumah" [confusion], meaning a confused mind:

Rashi on Gittin 70b:11:1.hebrew: ומי אמר שמואל - שחט בו שנים כותבין גט לאשתו, אלמא גט מחיים הוא:
Rashi on Gittin 70b:11:1.english: And did Shmuel say - [this, that if one] slit two [pipes] in him, they write a bill of divorce for his wife — thus [indicating that it is] a bill of divorce [given] while [he is] alive:

Rashi on Gittin 70b:11:2.hebrew: מעידין עליו - שמת, להשיא את אשתו:
Rashi on Gittin 70b:11:2.english: They may testify regarding him - that he died, [in order] to permit his wife to remarry:

Rashi on Gittin 70b:11:3.hebrew: חי הוא - וגיטו מחיים, אבל סופו למות, לכך מעידין עליו לאחר זמן להשיא את אשתו היכא דלא גירשה:
Rashi on Gittin 70b:11:3.english: He is alive - and [thus] his bill of divorce [is given] while [he is] alive, but he will ultimately die; therefore, they testify about him after some time to permit his wife to remarry, in a case where he did not divorce her:

Rashi on Gittin 70b:13:1.english: If that is so - since he will ultimately die:

Rashi on Gittin 70b:13:2.english: [He] should be exiled on his account - [i.e.,] the one who slaughters him unintentionally:

Rashi on Gittin 70b:14:1.english: The wind made him senseless - And were it not for the wind, he would not have died:

Rashi on Gittin 70b:14:2.hebrew: הוא קירב את מיתתו - על ידי שפירכס, ונמצא שלא הרגו זה, אבל מכל מקום סופו למות:
Rashi on Gittin 70b:14:2.english: He brought his death closer - Through [the fact] that he convulsed, and it turns out that this [person] did not kill him, but in any event he was destined to die:

Rashi on Gittin 70b:16:1.hebrew: שיחיא דלאו לאו נקטיה - חולי של שגעון המלמדו תמיד להרכין ראשו בהרכנת לאו או הין, ואינו משיב על דברי שאלתם:
Rashi on Gittin 70b:16:1.english: The affliction of "no, no" took hold of him - An illness of madness that conditions him to constantly incline his head with a nod of "no" or "yes," and he is not responding to their questions:

Rashi on Gittin 70b:17:1.hebrew: בסירוגין - ממתינין בין הרכנה לשאילה שעה, וחוזרין ושואלין לו אותה שאילה עצמה:
Rashi on Gittin 70b:17:1.english: At intervals - We wait a while between [his] nodding and [the next] question, and [then] ask him that same question again:

Rashi on Gittin 70b:18:1.english: Alternating bowing [movements] - to bow and incline [his head] in this manner at intervals:

Rashi on Gittin 70b:18:2.hebrew: הכי גרסינן: "חד לאו ותרין הין, ותרין לאו וחד הין" - דכי הך שיחיא לא נקטיה:
Rashi on Gittin 70b:18:2.english: This is how we read [the text]: "One 'no' and two 'yeses,' and two 'nos' and one 'yes'" - for a convulsion like this would not seize him:

Rashi on Gittin 70b:19:1.hebrew: אומרים לו - כשבודקין אותו על לאו, שואלין לו אם מבקש דברים הראוין לו בימות החמה ועכשיו ימות הגשמים:
Rashi on Gittin 70b:19:1.english: They say to him - When they test him regarding [answering] "no," they ask him whether he wants things that are appropriate for him in the summer, while now [it is] the rainy season:

Rashi on Gittin 70b:1:1.english: Below the testicles - such as in his feet and in his lower legs:

Rashi on Gittin 70b:1:2.english: Above the testicles - [That is,] on the shoulders, on the neck, and on the arm:

Rashi on Gittin 70b:20:2.english: And sheets - [asking] whether they should cover him with linen sheets in the rainy season:

Rashi on Gittin 70b:20:3.hebrew: דלמא קורא אחדיה - בימות החמה, ואע"פ שמשיב הין על הגלופקרין, לאו שוטה הוא:
Rashi on Gittin 70b:20:3.english: Perhaps a chill seized him - in the summer, and even though he answers "yes" regarding the warm coats, he is not an imbecile:

Rashi on Gittin 70b:3:1.hebrew: כותבין ונותנין גט לאלתר - ואפילו בתוך חוליו, הואיל ואמר קודם לכן, ולא אמרינן שוטה הוא ואינו יכול לגרש:
Rashi on Gittin 70b:3:1.english: They write and give a bill of divorce immediately - Even during his illness, since he said [so] beforehand, and we do not say [that] he is mentally incompetent and cannot divorce:

Rashi on Gittin 70b:4:1.english: To consult with him - To ask permission:

Rashi on Gittin 70b:6:1.hebrew: האי מחוסר מעשה - שצריך רפואה, בשרא סומקא אגומרי:
Rashi on Gittin 70b:6:1.english: This [one] is lacking an action - for he requires a remedy: red meat [roasted] on coals.

Rashi on Gittin 70b:7:1.english: His remedy is not in our hands - The medicine for his healing is not in our hands:

Rashi on Gittin 70b:9:1.hebrew: מגויד - מחותך בחתיכות, לשון "גודו אילנא" (דניאל ד):
Rashi on Gittin 70b:9:1.english: Severed [meguyad] - Cut into pieces; [from the same] expression as "cut down the tree" [godu ilana] (Daniel 4).

Tosafot on Gittin 70b:10:1.hebrew: התם דעתא צילותא היא - לא ידע רבינו יצחק עד מתי יחשב דעתא צילותא, דליכא למימר דבדקוהו בשעת נתינת הגט, דאם כן לא הוה פריך מידי לרבי יוחנן; ושמא עד שיודע שנטרפה דעתו יחשב דעתא צילותא. ובגט שכיב מרע אומר ר"י דצריך ליזהר שלא יתקלקל בין כתיבה לנתינה; דאם נתקלקל בינתיים, אפילו נתפקח לבסוף, אין מועיל אפי' לריש לקיש, דהא לא סמיה בידיה. ופעמים ששכיב מרע אינו בדעתו, ומספקא אי חשבינן ליה כשוטה, או שמא תונבא בעלמא הוא דנקטיה, וכישן דמי:
Tosafot on Gittin 70b:10:1.english: There, his mind is lucid - Rabbeinu Yitzchak does not know until when [his] mind is considered lucid; for one cannot say that they examine him at the time of the giving of the bill of divorce, since if so, [the Gemara] would not have raised any objection against Rabbi Yochanan. Perhaps until it becomes known that his mind has become deranged, [his] mind is considered lucid. And regarding a bill of divorce of a person on his deathbed, Rabbeinu Yitzchak says that one must be careful that [his mental state] does not deteriorate between the writing and the giving; for if it deteriorated in the interim, even if he regained lucidity at the end, it is of no avail even according to Reish Lakish, since his cure is not in his hand. And there are times when a person on his deathbed is not in his right mind, and it is uncertain whether we consider him like a mentally incompetent person, or whether it is merely a stupor that has seized him, and he is like one who is sleeping:

Tosafot on Gittin 70b:12:1.hebrew: ואי סלקא דעתך חי הוא אמאי מעידין כו' - דסלקא דעתך דמעידין עליו שכבר מת קאמר, ומשני: חי וסופו למות לאלתר, קודם שיתירוה ב"ד לינשא:
Tosafot on Gittin 70b:12:1.english: And if it enters your mind [that] he is alive, why do they testify, etc. - [The Gemara asks this] because it entered [the questioner's] mind that [the Mishnah] is saying that they testify about him that he has already died; and [the Gemara] answers [that he is] alive, and will ultimately die immediately, before the court permits her to marry:

Tosafot on Gittin 70b:13:1.hebrew: אלא מעתה יהא גולה על ידו - לשמואל פריך, דכיון דקאמר דמת לאלתר, היה לו לגלות. ולאו אשינויא ד"חי הוא וסופו למות" פריך, דכ"ש אי חשבת ליה כבר מת דקשה טפי; דקס"ד דגלות תלי במת לאלתר, ואם לא מת לאלתר אינו גולה. דס"ד דבהכי תלי, דלישנא דכתיב גבי גלות, "ויפל עליו וימות" (במדבר ל״ה:כ״ג), משמע ליה לאלתר; אע"פ שבמזיד חייב אפילו לא מת לאלתר, יש חילוק בין מיתה לגלות, כדמפלגי בגלות בין דרך ירידה לדרך עליה, ובמזיד אין שום חלוק. ולית ליה השתא הא דפריך באלו נערות (כתובות דף לג:): ממאי דבמזיד, ו"נקה המכה" מקטלא? ודלמא בשוגג, ומאי "ונקה" — מגלות! דמשמע דחייב גלות אפילו לא מת לאלתר:
Tosafot on Gittin 70b:13:1.english: If that is so, he should be exiled on his account - [The Gemara] is asking against Shmuel, for since he says that [the victim] is [considered] dead immediately, [the killer] should be exiled. And it is not asking against the answer, "He is alive and will eventually die," because all the more so if you consider him already dead, it is more difficult; for [the questioner] presently assumes that exile depends on dying immediately, and if he did not die immediately, he is not exiled. For [the questioner] assumes that it depends on this, because the phrasing written regarding exile, "and it fell upon him and he died" (Numbers 35:23), implies to him immediately; even though with intentional [murder] one is liable [to execution] even if [the victim] did not die immediately, there is a distinction between execution and exile, just as they distinguish in [the laws of] exile between a downward motion and an upward motion, whereas with intentional [murder] there is no distinction. And [the questioner] does not currently hold [in mind] that which [the Gemara] asks in [the chapter entitled] Eilu Na'arot (Ketubot 33b): "From where [do we know] that [the verse refers to] intentional [assault], and 'the striker shall be cleared' [means cleared] from execution? Perhaps [it refers to] unintentional [assault], and what does 'he shall be cleared' [mean]? [Cleared] from exile!" — which implies that one is liable to exile even if [the victim] did not die immediately:

Tosafot on Gittin 70b:14:1.hebrew: חיישינן שמא הרוח בלבלתו - דווקא בגלות חיישינן להני טעמי, אבל במזיד לעולם חייב; ושמא יש שום דרשא גבי גלות, כמו שיש חילוק בין גלות למיתה לענין דרך ירידה ועליה. והא דמשמע באלו נערות (גם זה שם), כי מוקי "ונקה המכה" אשוגג דחייב גלות אפי' לא מת לאלתר — מיירי בביתא דשישא, וכגון דלא פירכס:
Tosafot on Gittin 70b:14:1.english: We are concerned that perhaps the wind made him senseless - Specifically with regard to exile are we concerned about these reasons, but in the case of intentional [killing], he is always liable; and perhaps there is some scriptural exposition regarding exile, just as there is a distinction between exile and the death penalty with regard to [killing by] way of descending and ascending. And that which is implied in [the chapter] Elu Ne'arot (also there), when it establishes "and the one who struck shall be cleared" as referring to an unintentional [killer], that he is liable to exile even if [the victim] did not die immediately — it is dealing with a marble house, and in a case where he did not convulse:

Tosafot on Gittin 70b:15:1.hebrew: בביתא דשישא או דלא פירכס - מר חשיב בלבול הרוח קירוב מיתה יותר מפרכוס, ומר חשיב פרכוס קירוב מיתה יותר מבלבול הרוח, ותרוייהו בעו שימות מחמת הרוצח ולא מחמת דבר אחר. אי נמי: מר חשיב פירכוס מחמת רוצח משום דכל אדם דרכו לפרכס מחמת שחיטה, ומר חשיב בלבול רוח מחמת רוצח משום דאתי ממילא. אי נמי: לא פליגי הני לישני, ואינו חייב אלא בביתא דשישא ולא פרכס, והש"ס מפרש נפקותא בין הנך טעמי:
Tosafot on Gittin 70b:15:1.english: In a marble house, or where he did not convulse - One [version] considers the disturbance of the wind [to be] a greater hastening of death than convulsing, and one considers convulsing [to be] a greater hastening of death than the disturbance of the wind; and both require that he die on account of the murderer and not on account of something else. Alternatively: one considers convulsing [to be] on account of the murderer, because it is normal for every person to convulse as a result of slaughter, and one considers the disturbance of the wind [to be] on account of the murderer, because it comes on its own. Alternatively: these [two] versions do not disagree, and he is only liable in a marble house where [the victim] did not convulse; and the Talmud is [merely] explaining the practical difference between these reasons:

Tosafot on Gittin 70b:19:1.hebrew: דבי רבי ישמעאל תנא - אין נראה לומר דפליגי, דבדיקה דמתני' למה לא תועיל? אלא דקתני בדיקה עדיפא טפי הכי, דליכא למימר ביה דשיחיא דלאו לאו או דהן הן נקטיה, שהיא חכמה גדולה; כיון שאינו טועה בין ימות החמה לימות הגשמים, אפילו בעינן שלשה לאו ושלשה הן, סירוגין לא בעי:
Tosafot on Gittin 70b:19:1.english: The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught - It does not appear [correct] to say that they disagree, for why would the examination of the Mishnah not be effective? Rather, [the Tanna] teaches an examination that is much better in this way, in that one cannot say about him that an involuntary movement of "no, no" or of "yes, yes" has seized him, for it is [a sign of] great intelligence — since he does not confuse the summer and the rainy season, even if we require three "no"s and three "yes"es, an alternating [pattern] is not required:

Tosafot on Gittin 70b:20:1.hebrew: וניחוש שמא קרירות אחדיה - ולמה לנו לחושבו כשוטה, ונאמר שאינו גט, ונעגן אשתו חנם:
Tosafot on Gittin 70b:20:1.english: And let us be concerned lest chills seized him - Why should we consider him an imbecile, and say that it is not a [valid] bill of divorce, and leave his wife chained [in marriage] for naught:

Tosafot on Gittin 70b:4:1.hebrew: דקתני אין בדבריו האחרונים כלום - מייתור הלשון דייק, דהוה ליה למימר "הרי אלו יכתבו ויתנו"; אי נמי, דייק מדלא תנא "אין צריך לבודקו פעם שניה", דהוה משמע שממתינים מיהא עד שישתפה:
Tosafot on Gittin 70b:4:1.english: As it teaches: His final statement is nothing - [Reish Lakish] infers [this] from the superfluous wording, for [the mishna] should have said, "These should write and give [it]"; alternatively, he infers [it] from the fact that [the mishna] did not teach, "It is not necessary to examine him a second time," which would have implied that they wait, at any rate, until he is healed:

Tosafot on Gittin 70b:8:1.hebrew: ומי אמר רבי יוחנן הכי והא אמר שמואל שחט בו שנים כו' - וא"ת: השתא דמדמי ליה לאחזו קורדייקוס, תקשי ליה מתני' דקתני: "מי שאחזו קורדייקוס ואמר 'כתבו גט לאשתי', לא אמר כלום", והכא בשחט בו שנים ואמר "כתבו", הרי אלו יכתבו ויתנו! י"ל, דהא פשיטא דבשעה שאמר "כתבו", אכתי דעתא צילותא היא ולא דמי לאחזו קורדייקוס; אבל קודם שיכתוב וינתן, יתחלש ויתקלקל, ועל שעת נתינה נראה לו לדמות לאחזו קורדייקוס, וקשה לרבי יוחנן דאמר "אין כותבין ונותנין עד שישתפה". הקשה הרב רבי אלחנן: דאמאי פריך לרבי יוחנן? לריש לקיש נמי תיקשי! דהא טעמא דריש לקיש באחזו קורדייקוס משום דסמיה בידיה, והכא דאין סמיה בידיה מודה ר"ל דאין כותבין ונותנין, דמדמי ליה לשוטה. ולספרים דלא גרסי "ומי אמר רבי יוחנן הכי", א"ש דפריך לתרוייהו; אי נמי, נקט רבי יוחנן משום דקאמר בהדיא "אין כותבין":
Tosafot on Gittin 70b:8:1.english: But did Rabbi Yoḥanan say this? Didn't Shmuel say: [If one] slit two [pipes] in him, etc. - And if you ask: Now that [the Gemara] compares him [whose pipes were slit] to one seized by kordiakos, why doesn't the Mishnah pose a difficulty for it, which teaches: "One who was seized by kordiakos and said, 'Write a bill of divorce for my wife,' has said nothing," whereas here, where [another] slit two [pipes] in him and he said, "Write [a bill of divorce]," [the law is that] those [present] should write and give [it]? One can answer: For it is obvious that at the time he said, "Write," his mind is still clear, and he is not comparable to one seized by kordiakos; however, before it is written and given, he will grow weak and deteriorate [mentally], and with respect to the time of giving it seemed [appropriate] to [the Gemara] to compare [him] to one seized by kordiakos, and it is difficult for Rabbi Yoḥanan, who says: "We neither write nor give [the bill of divorce] until he recovers." The Rav, Rabbi Elḥanan, raised a difficulty: Why does [the Gemara] ask [only] against Rabbi Yoḥanan? Let it also be a difficulty for Reish Lakish! For Reish Lakish's reason in [the case of] one seized by kordiakos is because its remedy is in our possession, whereas here, where its remedy is not in our possession, Reish Lakish concedes that we neither write nor give [it], since he compares him to an imbecile. According to the texts that do not read "But did Rabbi Yoḥanan say this," it works out well, as [the Gemara] is asking against both of them; alternatively, it mentioned Rabbi Yoḥanan because he stated explicitly, "We do not write [it]":

Tosafot on Gittin 70b:8:2.hebrew: ורמז ואמר כתבו גט לאשתי - כגון שאמרו לו: "נכתוב גט לאשתך?" והרכין בראשו. ושמא אין צריך לבודקו כמו במתניתין, משום דאית ביה דעתא צילותא, כדאמרינן בסמוך:
Tosafot on Gittin 70b:8:2.english: And he signaled and said: Write a bill of divorce for my wife - For example, [where] they said to him, "Shall we write a bill of divorce for your wife?" and he nodded his head. And perhaps it is not necessary to examine him as in the Mishnah, because he has a clear mind, as [the Gemara] says shortly:
